retrieve: Steady, fast enough that the blades thump. Burn it in warm water. Figure-8 wide and fast.
whenNot: Below 55°F fish will not chase it; go to gliders or rubber.
yourJob: Count the cadence; if his blades stop thumping the retrieve is too slow.

retrieve: Medium steady. Lets you cover a flat fast and read where fish are.
whenNot: When follows are lazy; downsize to a glider instead.
yourJob: This is the search bait. Mark every follow on the map.

retrieve: Side to side with pauses over weed flats. Dawn, dusk, and calm overcast days.
whenNot: Chop over 10 mph or water under 58°F.
yourJob: Net ready at all times; topwater hits are visible and sudden.

retrieve: Slow steady, a straight line of noise. Night and dusk.
yourJob: Watch behind the lure for the wake of a follower.

retrieve: Short rod pulls with slack between. Glides side to side. Long pauses as water cools.
whenNot: Over thick weed tops; it fouls.
yourJob: Say when the lure comes into view so he can set up the 8 early.

retrieve: Rip down, let it rise. The rise is the trigger. Slower and longer pauses in cold water.
whenNot: When fish follow fast and hot; speed up with a bucktail.
yourJob: Keep the boat still during pauses.

retrieve: Twitch and pause along weed edges and breaks. Runs 4 to 8 ft.
whenNot: Over the tops of shallow weeds.
yourJob: Watch the sonar depth and call out when the edge drops.

example: Deep crankbait for trolling (Believer, Ernie type)
retrieve: Troll 2.5 to 4 mph along breaks and over the basin where cisco or perch show. Depth from line out.
yourJob: Watch rod tips for a change in throb; weeds kill the action.

retrieve: Pull and fall. Count it down to the fish's depth. Slow in cold water.
whenNot: Weeds that are still thick and standing.
yourJob: Count the fall out loud so he can repeat the depth.

example: Musky spinnerbait, single or double blade
retrieve: Slow roll through and over weeds; helicopter it down the edge. Fishes dirty water and wind.
whenNot: Flat calm clear water where fish see the wire.
yourJob: Keep the boat upwind; this is the wind bait.

example: Live sucker, 12 to 16 inch, on a quick-strike rig
retrieve: Under a float or on a slow drag off the break while casting another rod. Set the hook on the strike, not after a wait. Quick-strike rigs are what make release possible.
whenNot: Water over 58°F: suckers die fast and the artificial bite is better.
yourJob: Watch the float. The moment it moves, say so. Have the net and cutters in hand.

retrieve: Same as the big glider, smaller and slower. The downsize bait after follows.
whenNot: As a search bait; it covers water slowly.
yourJob: Tie it on before we need it.
